name: Low-Frequency RFID Cloning
description: 125kHz RFID systems — HID Prox, EM4100, HID H10301 — are the most common access control technology in commercial buildings and one of the most vulnerable. Low-frequency credentials can typically be cloned in seconds using a Proxmark3 or Flipper Zero. The cloned credential is written to a T5577 emulation card or RFID bracelet and replayed at the target reader. LF cloning requires only a few seconds of proximity to the target card.

blue.det: Credential used at unusual time or location; cloned credential used simultaneously with original; anti-passback violation.
blue.cm: Migrate to 13.56MHz HF or OSDP-encrypted systems; anti-skimming card sleeves; monitor access logs for duplicate concurrent credential use.
